definition: The period of decline following a peak; the phase after the highest point of strength, growth, or flourishing has passed.
etymology: From Greek para, meaning beside or beyond, and akme, meaning the highest point or peak — the same akme that gave English acme. Greek physicians used paracme to describe the stage of a fever after it breaks and begins to subside. The word traveled through Latin medical texts before quietly retiring from common use, waiting to be rediscovered.
usage: June 12 sits just nine days before the solstice, that brief acme of light, after which the year tips almost imperceptibly into its own paracme — the days still long and warm, but the sun already beginning its slow, reluctant retreat.
